{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
sales = pd.read_csv('data/sales.csv')

# Find the indices of the rows where 'status' is 'completed' and 'revenue' is NaN
invalid_revenue_indices = sales[(sales['status'] == 'completed') & (sales['revenue'].isna())].index

# Now, get the raw 'revenue' strings at those indices
raw_revenue_values = sales.loc[invalid_revenue_indices, 'revenue']

# Convert to list to inspect
raw_revenue_list = raw_revenue_values.tolist()
print("Raw revenue values for the 6 invalid rows:", raw_revenue_list)

# Manually inspect one
print("First value as string:", repr(raw_revenue_list[0]))

# Try to manually convert one after stripping
example_clean = raw_revenue_list[0].strip()
print("After stripping:", repr(example_clean))

# Check if they are all '0.00' (with possible invisible characters)
all_zero = all(val.strip() == '0.00' for val in raw_revenue_list)
print("Are all values '0.00' after stripping?", all_zero)

# Now, try to convert the entire 'revenue' column after cleaning
# Strip whitespace
sales['revenue_clean'] = sales['revenue'].str.strip()

# Replace any commas with dots (though we don't expect any)
sales['revenue_clean'] = sales['revenue_clean'].str.replace(',', '.', regex=False)

# Now convert to numeric
sales['revenue_clean'] = pd.to_numeric(sales['revenue_clean'], errors='coerce')

# Check how many values were recovered
recovered_count = sales['revenue_clean'].notna().sum() - sales['revenue'].notna().sum()
print("Number of revenue values recovered after cleaning:", recovered_count)

# Now, compute mean revenue for completed orders using the cleaned column
completed_orders_clean = sales[sales['status'] == 'completed']
mean_revenue_completed_clean = completed_orders_clean['revenue_clean'].mean()

# Print the result
mean_revenue_completed_clean"}
